questions.subject: MATH
questions.learningObjective: Solve problems involving karnaugh maps and minimization.
questions.stem: A Karnaugh map for a Boolean function of 8 variables has how many cells?

options.misconception: Wrong belief "uses a square grid sized by the variable count" gives 64, not 256.
Wrong belief "allocates two cells per variable" gives 16, not 256.
Wrong belief "doubles the required cells" gives 512, not 256.

questions.explanation: A Karnaugh map contains one cell per minterm, and 8 variables give 2 to the power 8 minterms, so it has 256 cells.
questions.hint: One cell per possible input combination.

provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.stem: A Boolean function of 6 variables is true on 47 assignments. How many cells of its Karnaugh map contain a zero?

Wrong belief "counts every cell as zero" gives 64, not 17.
Wrong belief "adds one extra zero cell" gives 18, not 17.

questions.explanation: The Karnaugh map has 2 to the 6 cells, of which 47 hold ones, leaving 17 cells holding zeros.
questions.hint: Subtract the one-cells from the total cell count.
